abstract: Adeno-associated virus vectors (AAVs) have broad utility in neuroscience. A variety of features, such as titer, capsid, enhancers and promoters, coding and non-coding elements, can be utilized to pursue diverse experimental ends. The net effects of titer and capsid have been used experimentally to pursue retrograde and anterograde studies, such as through the monosynaptic spread of high-titer AAV1. The literature on AAV8 is conflicting, with evidence for and against its long-range action outside of the infected starter population. Using the mouse corticopontocerebellar tract, we report that AAV8, when used at high titers, can be associated with long range recombination outside of the starter population. This phenomenon depended upon the viral titer and was influenced by the presence of other experimental injections. Surprisingly, separate injections of high-titer AAV8 recombinase and recombinase-reporter AAV8s gave rise to recombination across long distances in populations not known to be monosynaptically connected. Given the possibility of long range and emergent effects, we suggest that investigators empirically determine titer, capsid, and injection designs that reduce false positives and/or indirect effects.
